channel.title: Web & System Fundamentals :: FAU Cyber Security Club
channel.description: Most real-world vulnerabilities live at the intersection of web requests and system privileges. This section covers HTTP, how a browser-to-server conversation actually works, and the system-level concepts that make or break security.

item.title: HTTP
item.description: HTTP is the protocol browsers and servers use to communicate. Understanding it is non-negotiable for web security — every web vulnerability lives in an HTTP request or response. The Request-Response Model Every HTTP interaction is a request from a client and a response from a server. Both have a structure. Request: GET /login HTTP/1.1 Host: example.com Cookie: session=abc123 User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 Response:

item.title: System Concepts
item.description: Security vulnerabilities on the system level come down to a few recurring patterns: privilege misconfigurations, trusted environments running untrusted data, and processes with more access than they need. This page covers the concepts that underpin most of those patterns. Users and Groups Every process runs as a user. Every file is owned by a user and a group. Access is controlled by matching those identities.
